walkthroughs.body_html:
The fight to end slavery brought together very different people.

Roughly 12 million Africans were taken across the Atlantic in the whole transatlantic slave trade. By the 1780s many Britons saw this as a great evil.

Key campaigners included William Wilberforce, Olaudah Equiano, Thomas Clarkson, Granville Sharp and Quaker groups. ✋

Abolitionists used early forms of protest campaigning:

  • Huge petitions to Parliament
  • Books and pamphlets — including Equiano's autobiography
  • The sugar boycott — refusing to buy slave-grown sugar
  • Famous images, like the medallion 'Am I not a man and a brother?'

Their work slowly turned public opinion.

In 1807, Parliament passed the Slave Trade Act. British ships could no longer carry enslaved Africans.

In 1833, after more campaigning, Parliament passed the Slavery Abolition Act, ending slavery itself across most of the British Empire from 1834.

However, the £20 million compensation went to slave owners, not the freed people. Black communities are still pushing for fuller recognition today.

mcqs.q: Why did William of Normandy win the Battle of Hastings?
options: William won because he had gunpowder and the English did not.
Harold's exhausted army had just marched south after defeating the Norwegians at Stamford Bridge; William used feigned retreats and combined cavalry, infantry and archers.
Anglo-Saxons came as refugees fleeing the Vikings.
Harold lost because he was killed by an arrow in the eye early in the battle.

mcqs.q: How did Anglo-Saxons come to dominate post-Roman Britain?
options: A mix of migration from northern Germany and Denmark, settlement and intermarriage, and cultural absorption of Romano-British populations — not simple invasion and replacement.
Anglo-Saxons came as refugees fleeing the Vikings.
Anglo-Saxons invaded Britain and wiped out all the Romano-British inhabitants.
William won because he had gunpowder and the English did not.
